response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT ci.location AS location, COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) AS race_count FROM races r JOIN circuits ci ON ci.circuitId = r.circuitId WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM qualifying q WHERE q.raceId = r.raceId) GROUP BY ci.location), s AS (SELECT location, race_count, race_count * 1.0 / SUM(race_count) OVER () AS share FROM c), t AS (SELECT location, race_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT location, race_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_above_avg FROM t WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY share DESC

assumptions.assumption: A race 'has qualifying data' if at least one qualifying row exists for its raceId; each race is counted once per city.

The average share is taken across cities that have at least one race with qualifying data (cities with zero such races are not in the set of cities), so it equals 1 divided by the number of those cities.

alternatives.interpretation: The average share is taken across all circuit cities, including those with no races with qualifying data (share 0), which lowers the average.
alternatives.sql: WITH cities AS (SELECT DISTINCT location FROM circuits), cnt AS (SELECT ci.location AS location, COUNT(DISTINCT r.raceId) AS race_count FROM races r JOIN circuits ci ON ci.circuitId = r.circuitId WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM qualifying q WHERE q.raceId = r.raceId) GROUP BY ci.location), c AS (SELECT cities.location AS location, COALESCE(cnt.race_count, 0) AS race_count FROM cities LEFT JOIN cnt ON cnt.location = cities.location), s AS (SELECT location, race_count, race_count * 1.0 / SUM(race_count) OVER () AS share FROM c), t AS (SELECT location, race_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT location, race_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_above_avg FROM t WHERE share > avg_share ORDER BY share DESC
